subject: Reporting filters & role clarifications — serving runtime teams
body:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-11T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Proposal: reporting filters & role clarifications for serving runtime teams

Team —

I pushed a first-pass proposal attached (staff-map-v1.xlsx) that attempts to:
- Narrow scope overlap between the Kernel Runtime team and Continuous Batching team by introducing explicit "request routing" vs "kernel maintenance" filters.
- Clarify reporting lines for two senior ICs who are currently matrixed between Infra and Platform PMs.
- Identify 1:1 ownership for on-call rotations and escalation paths so SLOs are unambiguous.

Key asks:
1) Can each of you review the attached staff map and highlight operational risks (on-call gaps, SLO ownership, unresolved dotted lines) by EOD Wednesday?
2) Laura — can you draft a brief comms outline we can share with affected ICs and their managers?
3) Monica — HR will need a sensitive coordination plan for performance review impacts; please flag any constraints (notice periods, compensation calendars) that would affect timing.

Rationale in one line: reduce ambiguous handoffs that have caused repeated paging during incidents and muddy performance expectations.

Irene
Director, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachments: staff-map-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB), comms-draft.md (draft)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-12T11:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: reporting filters & role clarifications for serving runtime teams

Thanks, Irene — good start. Quick notes from my side after a skim:
- The proposed split of "request routing" vs "kernel maintenance" makes sense, but we need to be explicit about escalation ownership during multi-GPU storms (who owns cross-pod throttling decisions).
- Performance review risk: two folks in scope are up for calibration in mid-February. Monica, if we change their scope now, can we avoid impacting calibration outcomes? If not, what's the recommended window?
- Ops impact: we should run the new on-call schema as a shadow for one full sprint before making it primary. Suggest we scope a pilot for Q1.

I'll review the sheet in detail by tomorrow and mark rows with high/medium/low risk.

— Aditya
VP, Platform Engineering

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-13T09:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: reporting filters & role clarifications for serving runtime teams

Irene / Aditya —

I put together a short comms draft (attached as comms-draft.md) aimed at minimizing anxiety:
- Announcement opening: why change (incidents + unclear performance expectations)
- What changes (simple bullets showing reporting + on-call ownership per role)
- What won't change (comp cycles, managers, comp bands)
- Timeline: shadow pilot (Q1 sprint 1), review (end of sprint 2), official switch (end of Q1)
- People support: 30-minute 1:1s with each affected IC + manager, opt-in role transition checklist

Couple of practical asks:
1) Can we keep the two affected senior ICs out of public comms until they have 1:1s?
2) Monica — are there payroll cutoff concerns if we alter role titles before January?

If all agree, I can finalize and we can share a private note with the managers tomorrow.

Laura
Head of Product Operations

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Bcc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-14T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: reporting filters & role clarifications for serving runtime teams

All —

HR perspective and constraints:
- Compensation cycles: any title or scope changes submitted to payroll after the January 10 cutoff will not appear on the February cycle. If we need changes reflected in Feb calibration, we must complete approvals by Jan 8 and submit to payroll Jan 9.
- Performance review timing: moving scope mid-cycle is disruptive. Suggested path: keep formal performance scope as-is for FY26 reviews and use the shadow pilot to gather objective signals (pager reduction, incident MTTR, cross-team tickets closed). Then incorporate outcomes into role descriptions for FY27.
- Confidentiality: do not include affected individual names in manager-level comms until 1:1s are complete. Use manager-only queue with a confidential cover note.

Operational recommendation:
- Approve shadow pilot for Q1 (no formal role/title changes until after calibration).
- Final comms: manager-only brief next week; 1:1s during the following two weeks; public note end of January.

I'll prepare a short HR checklist and a suggested calendar and drop it in the Drive link you shared. Also looping in BrightWave contact (emma@brightwave.com) since they support our compensation ops tooling — cc'd on the thread for visibility.

Monica
Director, People Operations
Redwood Inference
